findings.issue: Wrote <RouterOutlet/> inside the route layout instead of <Slot/>, causing an SSR infinite-recursion/stack-overflow that cost ~15 turns to diagnose.
findings.suggestion: Copy the scaffolded starter's layout verbatim (it uses Slot) before replacing its markup, and check the starter's layout when the app renders duplicated chrome.

findings.issue: Two consecutive heredoc file writes failed because the target directories didn't exist; the same mistake repeated within 5 turns.
findings.suggestion: mkdir -p all route directories once, before the first route file write (or write files one at a time).

findings.issue: A single over-large batched bash write went wrong: stray mkdir of an unneeded [page] route, a broken heredoc, and a placeholder file with a wrong import.
findings.suggestion: Write one file per command; avoid stuffing directory creation plus multiple file bodies into one heredoc chain.

findings.issue: pkill -f 'vite preview' matched the invoking shell's own command line and killed it (exit 143), wasting a restart cycle.
findings.suggestion: Kill by recorded PID from /tmp/*.pid or use a pattern that can't match the current shell.

findings.issue: Several turns grepping Qwik City's dist internals and build plan for the SSR overflow without new information; the breakthrough came from inspecting rendered HTML two turns earlier.
findings.suggestion: When a render loop is suspected, dump the response body first and look for repeated landmarks before diving into framework internals.

findings.issue: A garbled no-op Python edit (SyntaxError: invalid decimal literal) burned a whole turn before being redone in trace.md:1503.
findings.suggestion: For small CSS edits, append the rule with a simple targeted command instead of multi-step replacement scripts.

summary: A well-run session: thorough up-front reading of spec, tests, data and screenshots; a mostly linear build with systematic debugging of the one hard bug (SSR layout recursion) and cause-level fixes for the three failing tests. The main waste was self-inflicted shell sloppiness in file writing and process management (~10-15 turns), not planning or reasoning problems.
